cells.tense: You are here with the pen, and both demands are being held without a fight.
cells.act: do the giving in the open this time, where it was always done unseen
cells.ask: Move a piece of care you'd normally keep off to the side into the open, done for someone in particular, where they can watch. When it's finished, stop, rather than quietly resuming it.
cells.core:
When two things need tending at once, you can carry both, and you can see where each one sits beside the other. Nothing gets dropped, and nothing gets forced. From outside the situation the shape is clear to you — what's growing, what's stalled, what's about to need water. You've been doing this work with your hands in it and your eyes out of it.

What's ready now is to let some of that tending happen in view. Not because anything is owed — just that care done off to the side, on repeat, makes the care look like nothing from where the people stand. Move one piece into the open. When it's done, let it be done, rather than picking it back up the moment it's seen.
cells.sheetLine: You carry two things at once and see the whole shape.
cells.verb: tending what grows, in form, with decisive care
cells.place: outside the system, seeing across all of it

cells.tense: You will be braced for what happens next before any of what is here has finished arriving.
cells.act: savour the realised thing without reaching past it
cells.ask: Choose something you've built that's plainly finished. Use it as it stands, with nothing added and no next version waiting, and enjoy it without reaching for what comes after.
cells.core:
You read the whole picture early: what's needed, what's coming, what will want tending before anyone else has noticed it wants tending. That's real. In this stretch it's running ahead of what's actually here — the next demand gets handled in your head before the current one has landed, and often the demand you prepared for doesn't show up. Care has turned into keeping ahead.

The whole shape includes the parts that are already done, and those don't need more from you. Let one finished thing stand, and take pleasure in it as it is rather than as a step toward something. That isn't settling. It's the difference between tending and being unable to set anything down.

cells.tense: You were the one who kept it going back then, and that is still the door you are standing at.
cells.act: keep following the star after everything that has happened
cells.ask: Go on toward the thing you've kept hoping for, the one you'd choose again today. Keep moving at it with no proof coming, and take the movement itself as the point.
cells.core:
There's something you've been carrying a while, and the part of you that reads the whole shape has gone quiet. Up close, all you can see is what's still ahead — not the pattern, not where this sits in the bigger thing. You kept going. You're just not letting yourself see what that took.

That part doesn't come back by bearing down on it. It comes back sideways, from staying with what you already chose. Keep moving toward it with no sign of anything. The clarity gets fed by the continuing, not the other way around — so let the going be enough for now.
cells.sheetLine: You kept it going and can't see what that took.

cells.tense: The care is running the room right now, and your account of it is that you are just standing here.
cells.act: stand where the giving can be witnessed
cells.ask: Let someone watch you do the steady thing you handle for them quietly. Don't narrate it, don't circle back to it, and then carry on with whatever's next.
cells.core:
Things stay steady around you — money paid, arrangements made, the load carried — and if anyone asked, you'd say you're not really doing anything. You see the whole shape clearly, every layer of it, and from that view your own part looks like standing still. The people nearby have a different picture. They've been watching you work this whole time and haven't said so.

Nothing needs announcing. Let one person be able to see one piece of the work. This isn't for their sake — it's so that the work exists somewhere you can see it too, which is the only place it can stop being invisible to you.
cells.sheetLine: The ones nearby have been watching you work this whole time.
